A 27-year-old, right handed, Japanese woman presented with continuous bilateral severe pain in the lower limbs, followed by chronic widespread pain. At the age of 31, she began experiencing widespread muscle cramps and twitches in the lower limbs. At the age of 33, she developed muscular weakness and had difficulty in walking and swallowing.
Three months later, she was re-admitted because of exacerbation of muscle stiffness and painful spasms.

extractions.value: The paper focuses on the utility of ultrasonography in evaluating muscle contractions in SPS. The patient was seronegative for GAD65, amphiphysin, and VGKC antibodies. Ultrasonography showed persistent continuous involuntary muscle contractions, widespread at rest, mainly in appendicular muscles and less frequently in axial muscles. The most symptomatic muscles were the quadriceps femoris bilaterally. Total counts of muscle contractions decreased from 90 to 36 after treatment.
extractions.quote: Using ultrasonography, we observed persistent continuous and involuntary muscle contractions, without voluntary movements in the upper and lower limbs... the total counts of muscle contractions decreased from 90 to 36
